sliding-filament.def: The explanation of contraction in which thin filaments slide past thick filaments toward the center of the sarcomere, so the Z discs move closer while neither filament changes length. The I bands and H zone narrow; the A band keeps its width.

cross-bridge.def: A myosin head bound to actin, bridging from a thick filament to a thin filament. It exists only while the head is attached.

cross-bridge-cycle.def: The repeating sequence by which a myosin head moves a thin filament: the cocked head binds actin; releasing phosphate drives the power stroke, which pulls the thin filament toward the M line; a new ATP binding frees the head; and splitting that ATP recocks it. It runs while calcium is on troponin and ATP is available.

rigor-mortis.def: The stiffening of muscles after death: ATP runs out, calcium leaks into the sarcoplasm, and myosin heads bind actin but cannot detach, locking the filaments together. It starts within a few hours and passes off over one to three days as the proteins break down.
